title: Subgraphs channels reducer updating out of turn
version: unknown (body lists langchain-core 0.3.72; no langgraph version)
observed_behavior: Two compiled sibling subgraphs share the parent AgentState, including g_retry_count behind a custom increment reducer. subgraph_1's node returns {}, yet the parent reducer is called again for g_retry_count each super-step, so the retry loop stops after two iterations instead of three.
structure_focus: Compiled sibling subgraphs sharing the parent state and a custom reducer; subgraph output echoes untouched keys, re-invoking the reducer
notes: Open. The issue is about reducer semantics across the subgraph boundary: a compiled subgraph used as a node returns every key in its output schema, including keys none of its nodes wrote, and the parent treats the echoed value as a fresh write. A commenter reproduces this analysis. Classified framework because the reported misbehavior is in how subgraph echoes are merged, not in the loop shape; the fixture keeps the shared state, custom reducer, two children and the loop conditional edge.
